mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% over the last two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically has led to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the GDP growth is negative, or if the correlation between negative GDP growth and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last two months signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 5% over the last two months and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5%, it signals a weakening demand environment coupled with labor market stress, which historically has led to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 5% in 2 months and UNRATE > 5%
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of HOUST decline and UNRATE level on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 over the last two months signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment reacts to the negative economic signal.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% over the last month, it signals a tightening monetary policy coupled with inflationary pressure, which historically has led to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail and food services sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS shows positive growth, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
